An estimate is one realized number. An **estimator** is the rule that would produce an estimate from every possible sample, and its **sampling distribution** describes the estimates that rule would produce across repeated samples.

## An empirical repeated-sampling reference

We use the vowel measurements of Hillenbrand et al. ([1995](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.411872)), distributed here through [`phonTools::h95`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=phonTools) under the package's BSD 2-Clause terms. The study recorded 45 adult men, 48 adult women, 27 boys, and 19 girls producing the same 12 /hVd/ vowels. One row is one vowel token nested within a speaker.

The teaching table contains complete duration measurements. Its F2 and F3 columns include package-supplied imputations, but those columns play no role here. We focus on the 48 adult women producing /I/ in *hid*. Repeated samples draw speaker rows with replacement from these observed durations. We call this construction the **empirical sampling reference** (ESR). It is useful for studying estimator behavior conditional on the cohort, but it does not reconstruct recruitment from all American English speakers.

```{r}
#| label: load-hillenbrand-estimators
library(ggplot2)

vowels <- read.csv(
  "data/hillenbrand/vowels-complete.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
women_hid <- subset(vowels, speaker_type == "woman" & vowel == "I")
x <- women_hid$duration_ms
target_mean <- mean(x)
target_sd <- sqrt(mean((x - target_mean)^2))

stopifnot(nrow(women_hid) == 48L, !anyDuplicated(women_hid$speaker_id))

data.frame(
  speakers = length(x),
  empirical_mean_ms = target_mean,
  empirical_median_ms = median(x),
  empirical_sd_ms = target_sd,
  minimum_ms = min(x),
  maximum_ms = max(x)
)
```

## Estimators are random variables

For a sample $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, the sample-mean estimator is

$$
T(\mathbf X)=\overline X=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i.
$$

Before sampling, $T(\mathbf X)$ is a random variable. After observing one sample $\mathbf x$, $T(\mathbf x)$ is an estimate. A useful sampling distribution is described by its expectation and variance:

$$
\mathbb{E}[T(\mathbf X)]
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\operatorname{Var}[T(\mathbf X)].
$$

The following simulation uses the observed adult-women group size and a fixed seed. The resampling unit is a speaker row.

```{r}
#| label: simulate-hillenbrand-estimator
set.seed(20261018)
replicates <- 20000L
sample_size <- nrow(women_hid)
sample_means <- replicate(
  replicates,
  mean(sample(x, size = sample_size, replace = TRUE))
)

sampling_center <- mean(sample_means)
sampling_sd <- sd(sample_means)

stopifnot(abs(sampling_center - target_mean) < 0.25)

data.frame(
  replicates = replicates,
  sample_size = sample_size,
  target_mean_ms = target_mean,
  mean_of_estimates_ms = sampling_center,
  sampling_sd_ms = sampling_sd
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-hillenbrand-estimator
#| fig-cap: "Empirical sampling distribution of the mean /I/ duration from speaker-row resamples. The line marks the empirical cohort mean."
ggplot(data.frame(mean_ms = sample_means), aes(mean_ms)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 42,
                 fill = "grey75", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = target_mean, color = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Mean /I/ duration in a speaker resample (ms)", y = "Simulation density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

The estimates vary even though the empirical target remains fixed at `r sprintf("%.3f", target_mean)` ms. This distinction between response variation and estimator variation is the foundation for standard errors, bias, and confidence intervals.

## Check your understanding

1. Which object changes across the ESR draws, and which target remains fixed?
2. What is the resampling unit?
3. Why would resampling all twelve vowel rows independently break the speaker structure?
4. What population claim does this ESR not license?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The resampled speaker rows, and thus the estimated means, change across draws; the empirical cohort mean remains fixed. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The resampling unit is one adult-woman speaker row for /I/ in *hid*. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The twelve vowel measurements from one speaker are dependent. Row-wise resampling would separate measurements that belong to the same speaker. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. The ESR does not license a claim about all American English speakers or reproduce the study's recruitment process. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
